newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan airline profits up in first eight months.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan airline profits up in first eight months.

text.p: Morocco's state-owned airline, Royal Air Maroc (RAM), made a net profit of 74 million dirhams ($8.5 million) in the first eight months of 1996, carrying 1.8 million passengers.
A RAM spokeswoman told Reuters on Thursday that turnover, at 3.3 billion dirhams from January to August, was up 3.14 percent from 3.2 billion in the same period of 1995.

The company's 27 aircraft, mainly Boeings, carried 8.3 percent more passengers over the same period January-August last year, achieving an occupancy rate of 64.8 percent, an improvement of 1.15 points compared with the end of August 1995.
Most of the increased passengers -- 14.9 percent -- was on the airline's regular routings, to France, other parts of Europe, long-haul and domestic flights.
Charter traffic fell by 11.7 percent, the company said.
The Moroccan government owns 93 percent of the company. The remaining seven percent is held by Air France, the Spanish firm Iberia and private investors.
Officials earlier said the government would add RAM next year to the list of 72 state companies to be privatised by end 1998.
